title: Large File Handling with Git LFS
description: Use Git LFS to store large binary files outside your repository while keeping them versioned.

data.text: Git LFS (Large File Storage) replaces large files with tiny pointer files in your Git repository and stores the actual file contents on a remote LFS server. This keeps your repository small and fast while still versioning large files like images, videos, and compiled binaries.
Install Git LFS on your machine and initialize it in your repository. Git LFS is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

data.title: Install and initialize Git LFS
data.code:
# Install Git LFS (Windows: choco install git-lfs)
# macOS: brew install git-lfs
# Linux: apt-get install git-lfs

# Install the Git LFS filters
git lfs install

# Track large file types
git lfs track "*.psd"
git lfs track "*.zip"
git lfs track "*.mp4"
git lfs track "*.exe"

# Commit the .gitattributes file
git add .gitattributes
git commit -m "chore: configure Git LFS"

data.text: When you add a tracked file, Git LFS replaces it with a tiny pointer file (typically 100-200 bytes) in the repository. The actual file content is uploaded to the LFS server. When someone clones the repository, Git LFS downloads only the file contents they check out.

data.title: Git LFS pointer file example
data.code:
# Pointer file in Git (stored in repository)
version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1
oid sha256:4f8ac3b9c2a1d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e
size 52428800

# The actual 50MB file is stored on the LFS server
# not in the Git repository

# Clone and LFS downloads on checkout
git clone https://github.com/example/project.git
cd project

# When you access image.png, Git LFS downloads it
cat image.png > /dev/null

# LFS objects are stored in .git/lfs/

data.text: Git LFS integrates with standard Git commands. git push pushes both the pointer files and the LFS objects. git pull pulls both. No special commands are needed beyond the initial setup.

data.title: Push and pull with Git LFS
data.code:
# Add a large file
git add assets/banner.mp4

# Commit
git commit -m "chore: add banner video"

# Push — LFS uploads the file to the LFS server
git push origin main

# On another machine, clone and LFS downloads
git clone https://github.com/example/project.git
cd project

# LFS files download automatically on checkout
ls -lh assets/banner.mp4

# If LFS files are missing, fetch them
git lfs pull

data.text: If your repository already has large files committed, use git lfs migrate import to rewrite history and move existing large files to LFS. This rewrites all commits that reference the large files.

data.title: Migrate existing large files to LFS
data.code:
# Track the file type
git lfs track "*.zip"

# Migrate existing zip files to LFS
git lfs migrate import --include="*.zip"

# This rewrites history to replace zip files
# with LFS pointer files

# Force push the rewritten history
git push --force origin main

# Verify: check that zip files are now pointers
git show HEAD:assets/data.zip | head -1

# Output starts with:
# version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1

data.title: Rewriting LFS history requires force push
data.text: git lfs migrate import rewrites every commit that references the migrated files. This changes commit SHAs. Coordinate with your team before force-pushing to avoid disrupting others' work.

GitHub and GitLab provide free LFS storage and bandwidth, but with limits. GitHub provides 1 GB free storage and 1 GB free bandwidth per month. Exceeding these limits requires purchasing additional data packs.

data.title: Check LFS usage on GitHub
data.code:
# Check LFS usage in the GitHub web UI:
# Repository → Settings → Billing → Git LFS

# Or check with the GitHub CLI:
gh api repos/:owner/:repo/lfs/usage

# Monitor LFS object count
git lfs ls-files | wc -l

# Check LFS file sizes
git lfs ls-files --size

items.question: Can I use Git LFS without a hosted LFS server?
items.answer: Yes. You can run your own LFS server (e.g., lfs-test-server, git-lfs-server) or use a self-hosted GitLab instance with LFS support.

items.question: Does Git LFS work with GitHub Actions?
items.answer: Yes. GitHub Actions automatically handles LFS checkout with actions/checkout. Use with: lfs: true.

items.question: Can I lock files with Git LFS?
items.answer: Yes. Use git lfs lock <file> to prevent others from pushing changes to the same file. This is useful for binary files that cannot be merged.

items.question: What file types should I track with LFS?
items.answer: Track binary files: images (PSD, PNG, JPG), videos (MP4, MOV), archives (ZIP, TAR), and compiled artifacts (EXE, DLL). Do not track text files or source code with LFS.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Git LFS stores large files outside the repository as pointer files
git lfs track <pattern> defines which file types to store in LFS
git lfs migrate import rewrites history to move existing files to LFS
GitHub provides 1 GB free LFS storage and bandwidth per month
Use LFS for binary files; use normal Git for text and source code
